title: Monthly Prescription Limit on Paid Fills — Pharmacy Benefit
content:
**Network pharmacy clause.** Where the member's PrairieRx plan applies a monthly cap, a fill beyond the plan's monthly number of paid fills in the calendar month is rejected with the reject reason "monthly limit reached". Fills of exempt drug classes never count, and where the plan's cap counts brand drugs only, generic fills never count. A fill approved through a quantity limit exception for the monthly cap pays beyond the cap for the drug named in the exception until the exception's approved-through date.

### How the month's fills are counted

The count for a month is taken over the calendar month of the fill date, on the member's pharmacy coverage:

1. start from the paid fills on the coverage in that calendar month;
2. take away the fills that were reversed;
3. leave out fills whose drug is in an exempt drug class;
4. where the plan's cap counts brand drugs only, leave out preferred generic fills.

### Outcome table

| Plan applies a monthly cap | Counted paid fills already in the month | The next fill |
|---|---|---|
| No | any number | This clause does not reject it |
| Yes | fewer than the cap | Counts toward the cap and is not rejected by this clause |
| Yes | equal to the cap | Rejected, "monthly limit reached" — unless it is the drug named in an approved quantity limit exception for the monthly cap, on or before the exception's approved-through date |

### Worked example (hypothetical)

A plan's cap is 6 paid fills of all drugs. In one calendar month the member has 6 paid fills, one of which is a naloxone fill (exempt class) and one of which was later reversed. The counted fills are 6 less 1 exempt less 1 reversed, that is 4. The next fill is the fifth counted fill and is not rejected by the cap.

### Point of judgement

*A member has an approved quantity limit exception for the monthly cap on one drug.* Only that drug pays beyond the cap, and only until the approved-through date; other drugs remain under the cap.
